statement: Define V = {1, 2, ..., n}. Define E = { {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} : 0 ≤ i < len(edges) }. For v in V, define deg(v) = |{ e in E : v ∈ e }|. The function returns a result r and r = true if and only if there exists a set F of unordered pairs of distinct vertices from V such that: (1) |F| ≤ 2; (2) every pair in F is not in E; (3) the pairs in F are pairwise distinct; (4) for every v in V, deg(v) + |{ e in F : v ∈ e }| is even.
preconditions: n is a machine integer with 3 ≤ n ≤ 100000. edges is a list with 2 ≤ len(edges) ≤ 100000. For every i with 0 ≤ i < len(edges), len(edges[i]) = 2, and 1 ≤ edges[i][0] ≤ n, 1 ≤ edges[i][1] ≤ n, and edges[i][0] ≠ edges[i][1]. For every i,j with 0 ≤ i < j < len(edges), the unordered pairs {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} and {edges[j][0], edges[j][1]} are distinct.

statement: Define V = {1,...,n}, E = { {edges[i][0],edges[i][1]} : 0 <= i < len(edges) }, deg(v) = |{ e in E : v in e }|, and O = { v in V : deg(v) is odd }. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = false if and only if at least one of the following holds: (a) |O| > 4; (b) |O| = 2 with O = {a,b} and {a,b} in E and, for every w in V with w != a and w != b, {a,w} in E or {b,w} in E; (c) |O| = 4 with O = {a,b,c,d} pairwise distinct and none of (i) {a,b} not in E and {c,d} not in E, (ii) {a,c} not in E and {b,d} not in E, (iii) {a,d} not in E and {b,c} not in E. This is the complete structural characterisation of the false case (the missing complement of spec_1, making the trickiest sub-case explicit).
